name: Hair of the Dog Barbershop - Bar

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: The baffles of the ice machine were observed accumulated with pink slime on the food contact surfaces. The owner mentioned that the baffles are cleaned every two months professionally. Discussed possibly cleaning the baffles more frequently (once a month). Ensure that ice baffles are cleaned as frequent as necessary to prevent buildup and contamination of ice.
findings.citation_text:
4-602.11(E) Equipment Food-Contact Surfaces and Utensils. (E) Except when dry cleaning methods are used as specified under § 4-603.11, surfaces of UTENSILS and EQUIPMENT contacting FOOD that is not TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be cleaned:
(1) At any time when contamination may have occurred; (2) At least every 24 hours for iced tea dispensers and CONSUMER self service UTENSILS such as tongs, scoops, or ladles; (3) Before restocking CONSUMER self-service EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS such as condiment dispensers and display containers; and (4) In EQUIPMENT such as ice bins and BEVERAGE dispensing nozzles and enclosed components of EQUIPMENT such as ice makers, cooking oil storage tanks and distribution lines, BEVERAGE and syrup dispensing lines or tubes, coffee bean grinders, and water vending EQUIPMENT: (a) At a frequency specified by the manufacturer, or (b) Absent manufacturer specifications, at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.comment: There weren’t any quaternary ammonia test strips available at the facility. The owner mentioned that the facility used the last of their test strips. Quat test strips were provided to the facility to correct the violation. Ensure that quat test strips are available to be sure that concentrations are at the manufacturer’s recommendation.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.116 Warewashing Equipment, Determining Chemical Sanitizer Concentration. Concentration of the SANITIZING solution shall be accurately determined by using a test kit or other device.

findings.title: Food handler training
findings.comment:
There are currently two employees hired to operate the bar area. One employee has a food handler certificate, while the other employee does not have a food handler certificate. Discussed with the owner that anyone that handles ice will need to obtain food handler certificates. Ensure that all bartenders are food handler certified. 

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
findings.citation_text:
2-102.11 (A), (B) & (C)(1), (4)-(16) Priority violations were observed for handwashing, bare hand contact with ready to eat foods, cross contamination, proper use of chemicals, and source (risk classification). See violations 8, 9, 11, 15, & 28 for details. Active managerial controls were discussed. All priority and priority foundation violations were corrected at time of inspection. 
Based on the risks inherent to the food operation, during inspections and upon request the PIC shall demonstrate to the regulatory authority knowledge of foodborne disease prevention, application of the hazard analysis and critical control points, and the requirements of the Code.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.citation_text:
2-103.11 (O) Signed copies of employee health reporting agreements were not available. Employees were not familiar with employee health policy requirements. Employee health documents were provided and policy was discussed with emphasis on knowledge required by management and staff on reporting illness and time frame for exclusion from food handling depending on reportable symptoms versus being diagnosed with and/or potentially exposed to foodborne pathogens. Employees present at time of inspection signed reporting agreements. Extra copies of reporting agreement were provided for bar manager to sign one as well. Ensure all staff are educated on the employee health policy upon hiring and sign reporting agreements prior to beginning their first shift. Maintain signed copies of reporting agreements for staff.
The person in charge shall ensure that food employees are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with law, to the person in charge, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through food, as specified under  2-201.11(A).

findings.title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events
findings.citation_text:
2-501.11 Written procedure with specific actions to be taken in case of a vomit and/or diarrhea incident was not available. Norovirus disinfection handout was provided. Bleach is available for use (barbershop side). Maintain the norovirus disinfection policy on-site along with all other employee health documentation.
A food establishment shall have written procedures for employees to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the food establishment. The procedures shall address the specific actions employees must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of employees, consumers, food, and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.14 Bartender did not wash hands prior to preparing beverages for customers. Bartender was observed touching general surfaces and preparing sanitizer solution in a spray bottle prior to handling cups and garnish for beverages. Handwashing between tasks was discussed, and bartender was observed washing hands between tasks for remainder of inspection. Ensure hands are washed properly prior to making drinks, especially after handling chemicals and doing other general tasks.
Food Employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles. Employees shall also wash their hands after engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

findings.title: No bare hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed
findings.citation_text:
3-301.11 (B) 1. Scoop was observed in ice bin with the handle down in contact with ice. Ice scoop was positioned to allow for proper storage with handle up out of ice. Proper storage of ice scoop was discussed. 
2. Bartender had bare hand contact with citrus garnish placed on a customer’s glass. Use of gloves or tongs to handle drink garnish was discussed. Gloves were said to not currently be available but should be purchased to handle citrus and other ready to eat foods during preparation. Tongs are available to handle garnishes once prepared for use. Bartender located single use food service gloves and placed them at the bar for use during inspection.
Except when washing fruits and vegetables as specified under §3-302.15 or as specified in (D) and (E) of this section, food employees may not contact exposed, ready-to-eat food with their bare hands and shall use suitable utensils such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing equipment.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.citation_text:
5-205.11 Handwashing sink at bar was used as a dump sink and contained ice, citrus garnish and stir straws. Proper use of the handwashing sink was discussed, and sink was cleaned out during inspection. Use of the middle basin at the 3 part sink for multiple tasks was discussed as well as maintaining a strainer with a bucket as a dump location. 
Handwashing sinks are to be accessible at all times and used only for handwashing. Cease using the handwashing sink for anything other than handwashing.

findings.title: Food obtained from approved source
findings.citation_text:
3-201.11 Facility has been operating as a medium risk operation with a low risk permit based on observations and discussion with bartender. Upon arrival inspector observed a pizza oven and hotdog roller on a cabinet located at the north wall in the seating area. Hotdogs were said to be self-service like frozen pizzas, with customers preparing their own food when hotdogs are out for service. Hotdogs require an upgrade to medium risk classification regardless of customer self-service. Frozen pizza self-service is the only exception to maintain low risk classification for food service. Pizzas are sold to customers, and customers use the pizza oven located in seating area to bake their own pizza. Hotdog roller was shut off, and bartender stated they would leave it off for the remainder of operations. No hotdogs were on the roller for service at the time of inspection. Bartender spoke with the owner prior to conclusion of inspection. Hotdog roller was removed from the seating area and will be removed from the facility. Nothing other than frozen pizzas for self-service will be served at this time.
Food shall be obtained from sources that comply with the law.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.citation_text:
3-304.11 Glass jars with citrus garnish were sitting in direct contact with ice intended for consumption. Jars were moved and a layer of ice was removed for discard. The outer surfaces of containers are not considered clean and should not be stored in ice used for beverages. 
Food shall only contact equipment and utensils that are cleaned and sanitized as specified in Parts 4-6 and 4-7 of this Code; single-service and single-use articles; and linens, such as cloth napkins, as specified under § 3 304.13 that are laundered as specified under Part 4-8 of this Code.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-602.11 (E) Mold was starting to accumulate on the lower edge of the ice machine baffle in the ice bin, especially under ledge used for ice scoop storage. The wall to the right behind the baffle also appeared to have some general buildup. Ensure cleaning occurs in the ice bin and along the baffle between detail cleanings of the ice maker.
Equipment such as ice machine bins and ice makers shall be cleaned at a frequency specified by the manufacturer, or absent manufacturer specifications, at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil or mold

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.citation_text:
7-202.12 Unlabeled spray bottle of pink liquid was said to contain sanitizer. Product tested at a concentration that did not register on the ppm chart of inspector’s test strips. Sanitizer appeared to possibly be concentrated product with little to no water added for dilution. Required concentration of product used is 200ppm. Solution was remade to be at 200ppm, and spray bottle was labeled as to the contents. Ensure proper use of sanitizer per product label directions. 
Chemical sanitizers must meet the concentration and use requirements specified by 40 CFR 180.940. Toxics shall be used according to the manufacturer's use directions included in labeling, and must not be used in a manner that poses a health hazard or potential risk of cross contamination.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.citation_text:
4-302.14 Bartender could not locate a quat test kit at time of inspection. Owner provided a quat test kit prior to conclusion of inspection. 
A test kit that accurately measures the concentration of sanitizing solutions in mg/L shall be provided.

findings.title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices
findings.citation_text:
5-205.15 Cold water pressure was minimal at the bar handwashing sink allowing for a small stream of water. Provide repairs to allow for adequate water pressure for both hot and cold running water at the bar handwashing sink.
A plumbing system shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625  Sec. 3.06 Proof of food handler certification was not available for employee working at time of inspection. Ensure all staff complete the online food handler course. New employees have 30 days from the date of hiring to complete certification. Copies of certifications need to be maintained on-site.
All food handlers, other than someone who has a food manager certification, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code.
